Hi Saptarsi, I have a couple of queries inline.
USB isn't the only point-to-point protocol (not requiring a bus address) - we have the serial binding too. I think this can just be `interface` like in the constructor above.
Acknowledged
Why? We already have the `interface` member above.
Acknowledged
Nit: The comment seems unnecessary, remove?
Acknowledged
Still needed?
Acknowledged
This NOLINT can now go away
Acknowledged

Hello Saptarshi,

Some suggestions on interface name validity check
Some minor suggestions
Should we add check for Interface name if its a valid mctp device or not?
Acknowledged
How would we do that if the interface name is an altname/alias?
An error should be propagated if the name isn't valid. Let's not add brittle pre-checks.
Acknowledged
Acknowledged, can check for `/sys/bus/usb/devices`
Better to check in `/sys/class/net/` for the interface to showup
Probably dont need to pass address from here and simply pass empty vector while passing argument for MCTPDevice constructor
Acknowledged

Please update the note section with dependency on gerrit patch which has schema change for MCTPUSBDevice

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/77381
Acknowledged

Can we avoid sending address altogether since its supposed to be an empty vector? we can pass as std::vector<uint8_t>{} argument when going to MCTPDDevice constructor

Also we can avoid sending it to MCTPUSBDevice object from .cpp file
Acknowledged

I think this change subject needs work. Please be specific.

```
mctpreactor: Support configuration for USB MCTP devices
```
Acknowledged

Is this a gerrit change number?

Please provide a proper URL instead.
Acknowledged

How do we know this is a USB device from the output here?

I don't think this has much value.
Acknowledged
Looks good to me
Can you please review https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/80593 ?
You need to match on the removal here.
Acknowledged
You shouldn't need a separate getConfiguration() call here. Instead you can add to the configuration list in the call on line 249.
Acknowledged
Looks good to me.
This needs to be reconciled with the feedback on the EM schema
Need to still figure out a way to make the bus number deterministic.
Done
Please push an update tyo https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/77381 as well.
Any reason why these are non-member functions? Not that that is wrong, but seems to deviate from the functions in I2CMCTPDevice, for ex.
Acknowledged

Would it be better to lookup the busnum attribute file instead? Is the `usb<bus_num>` pattern guaranteed to be there?
At the very least, please remove the hardcoded value 3 here and use something like std::string_view("usb")::length(), which would still be compile time evaluated

The busnum attribute would be inside the usb<bus_num> directory, so better to use this pattern usb<bus_num>instead, even though both would achieve the same functionality.
ACK, removing hardcoded value.
Acknowledged
Would be good to provide an example of what the sysfs path for the host controller/root looks like say on the AST2600
Acknowledged

Still don't think this is fool-proof. With the usbmon module enabled. I also get a directory called `usbmon` in the same path. That would break this code based on which entry the iterator returns first. Can we instead look for the busnum file within the said directory?
Acknowledged
CI failure seems unrelated to the patch...
Nit: This could be a map from the SOC family name to an array of the sysfs paths.
Just a note that this patch still tests fine post the changes I made to the related EM patches as part of rework.

There are 2 corner case that can cause mctp reactor daemon to exit with warning:
- no usb device found (possibility that the USB device is powering up or enumeration is delayed).
- USB hotplug after mctp reactor daemon started.
Binding the enablement to specific SOC may not be scalable as it restricts other HW supporting the feature from leveraging this mctp usb configuration.
Similar to SOC, rootHubPath too can change, hence restricting this to a few paths would limit the other rootHub (including in other SOC) from using this mctp usb configuration.
Can you add the description on how this port array is derived?

If there is no USB device that is MCTP capable then this will cause the flow to enter catch. better to nullptr in that case with error log rather than causing daemon to stop. 

There could be possibilities that USB device can be hot pluggable, and on daemon start it couldn't be found causing daemon to exit with a warning.
Apologize for the accidentally pushed, please refer to PS34 for review.
Apologizes for the accidentally pushed, has reverted to the original patch.
